new_fragment:
The corrected four-worker comparison loads the same retained ordinary Mathlib
native library in both paths, without the counterexample wrapper or external
oracle. Table~\ref{tab:corrected-warm-resource} reports its complete warm cell
on the original 7,808 miniF2F candidates, under the same CPUs 8--11,
48~GiB sampled aggregate RSS budget, unlimited per-process address space
and 300-second admitted-attempt allowance.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{lr}
\toprule
Warm-cell measure & Observed value \\
\midrule
Accepted candidates & 3,014 \\
Rejected candidates & 4,668 \\
Timeouts & 85 \\
Resource failures & 41 \\
External whole elapsed (s) & 25,176.49 \\
Internal whole elapsed (s) & 25,175.27 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Complete corrected four-warm resource baseline for all 7,808 original
miniF2F candidates. The corresponding engine cell is not yet complete, so the
table establishes neither accepted-set parity nor a comparative speedup.}
\label{tab:corrected-warm-resource}
\end{table}

The external clock covers launch, output and native retirement. Preparation
takes 3.03 seconds within the internal whole clock and is not added again.
The 7,808 ordinary attempts include 52 watchdog preemptions, each followed by
one exclusive retry. Those retries end in 41 resource failures and 11 timeouts,
and their serial admitted envelopes sum to 12,106.92 seconds.
Final resource failures retain attributed watchdog records rather than native
allocator exceptions. The one-second aggregate RSS observations peak at
48.77~GiB, including 93 over-budget samples and 93 recorded preemptions.
Sampling does not enforce a hard RSS quota.

Retry ordering remains a comparison boundary. The frozen warm adapter drains
ordinary peers for immediate resource retries, whereas the engine finishes its
registered ordinary frontier before exclusive retries. Any complete comparison
therefore measures these resource paths, including retry ordering, rather than
isolating copy-on-write.
